title: Underwater Seaweed Swaying with Buoyancy and Fluid Drag
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that simulates an underwater scene with procedural soft-body seaweed strands swaying under buoyancy and fluid drag forces.

## Scene Setup
- Dark blue-green background (color #0a2a3a) to simulate deep water.
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 4, 12), looking at origin.
- Lighting: One soft ambient light (color #2266aa, intensity 0.5) and one directional light (color #88ccff, intensity 0.8) from above-right (position 5, 10, 5).
- A sandy ground plane (color #8b7d5e, 20x20) at y=0.
- Add subtle animated particle sprites (small white dots, ~80 particles) drifting slowly upward to simulate underwater particulate, scattered randomly in a box from x:[-8,8], y:[0,10], z:[-8,8]. Each particle drifts upward at 0.02-0.05 units/sec and wraps back to y=0 when reaching y>10.

## Seaweed Soft-Body System
- Generate exactly 5 seaweed strands at x positions: [-3, -1.5, 0, 1.5, 3], all at z=0.
- Each strand is a chain of 8 segments (nodes), each segment length = 0.5 units.
- The bottom node (index 0) of each strand is pinned to the ground (fixed).
- Visualize each strand as a smooth green TubeGeometry or connected CylinderGeometry segments. Use color #1a8a2a for strands, with slight color variation per strand.
- Physics per node (Verlet integration):
  - Gravity: -2.0 in Y (reduced underwater gravity).
  - Buoyancy: +3.0 in Y (net upward force, so strands float upward naturally).
  - Fluid drag coefficient: 0.04 (applied as velocity damping: velocity *= (1 - drag)).
  - Current force: a global horizontal sinusoidal force in X = currentStrength * sin(time * currentFrequency), applied to all free nodes.
  - Default currentStrength = 1.0, default currentFrequency = 0.8.
- Distance constraints: after integration, enforce segment length constraints (iterative correction, 3 iterations per frame) so each segment stays at length 0.5.
- The tip node (index 7) should sway the most; the base should remain fixed.

## User Interactions
1. A slider labeled 'Current Strength' (range 0.0 to 3.0, step 0.1, default 1.0) controls currentStrength.
2. A slider labeled 'Current Frequency' (range 0.1 to 3.0, step 0.1, default 0.8) controls currentFrequency.
3. Press key 'B' to toggle a 'burst' mode: when active, apply an additional one-time impulse of +4.0 in X to all free nodes, then deactivate burst. This simulates a sudden current surge.
4. Press key 'R' to reset all seaweed strands to their initial straight upward positions and zero velocities.
5. Click on the canvas: cast a ray from the mouse position. If it intersects near any seaweed strand (within 1.0 unit of any node), apply a radial push force of magnitude 2.0 away from the click point to all nodes within range.

## HUD / UI
- Top-left overlay div showing:
  - 'Strands: 5'
  - 'Current: {currentStrength}' (updates live)
  - 'Frequency: {currentFrequency}' (updates live)
  - 'Burst: ON/OFF' (shows ON briefly for 0.5s after B press, then OFF)
  - 'Sim Time: {seconds}' (elapsed simulation time, 1 decimal)
- Sliders positioned at bottom-center of the screen.

## State Management (window.__3D_STATE__)
Expose the following on window.__3D_STATE__ and update every frame:
- strandCount: number (always 5)
- segmentsPerStrand: number (always 8)
- currentStrength: number (current slider value)
- currentFrequency: number (current slider value)
- burstActive: boolean (true during burst frame, false otherwise)
- simTime: number (elapsed seconds)
- strandTips: array of 5 objects {x, y, z} representing the world position of each strand's tip node (index 7)
- strandBases: array of 5 objects {x, y, z} representing the world position of each strand's base node (index 0)
- avgTipY: number (average Y of all 5 tip positions)
- maxTipDisplacementX: number (max absolute X displacement of any tip from its base X)
- particleCount: number (number of active particles)
- dragCoefficient: number (0.04)
- resetCount: number (how many times R has been pressed, starts at 0)
- clickPushCount: number (how many times a click-push was applied, starts at 0)
- nodesAreFinite: boolean (true if ALL node positions across all strands have finite x,y,z values — no NaN/Infinity)
physics_constraints: Verlet integration with buoyancy (+3.0 Y) exceeding gravity (-2.0 Y) so strands float upward. Fluid drag coefficient 0.04 damps velocity each frame. Distance constraints enforce 0.5 unit segment lengths with 3 solver iterations. Sinusoidal current force in X. All node positions must remain finite (no NaN/Infinity). Tips should generally be above bases due to net buoyancy.
